Metres and Ratio preserve finite physical/dimensionless values, Count owns u16 representation, while shape/product-specific admissibility and computed geometry still need appropriate owners.

Recipe/component validation enforces one parent, numeric and sampling constraints, but finite Ratio and lower belly bound alone do not ensure a bounded generated transverse extent. Direct construction and decoder policy remain open.

Derived width multiplies width, taper/plan and finite belly; operations can escape nominal input or frame bounds. Face and sampling paths reject some invalid values/budgets, but no blanket accepted-output conclusion follows.

Attachment frame location, originating component and complete orientation need coherent association; independent keyed maps and alias owner can lose that relationship in the already recorded q127 scenario.
Existing attachment frame and blade profile concepts have distinct ownership from axial range, a transverse bound, recipe identity and model output. No one wrapper is presumed to solve all.
Global grip alias point and owner-ID rotation are independently retained; owner lookup from alias text can disagree with actual component. Historical frame finding already owns this, not a new count.
Three historical source objects individually equal 6533 and 95e. Dirty pr-working snapshot and uninspected connected code preclude a whole-tree or runtime equivalence assertion.

BladePlan and BladeCrossSection are closed separate enums; optional fuller and point express absent modes but their combination is checked by the profile validator. No missing-field or blanket optionality defect inferred.

LoftedBladeParameters derive serialization with explicit deny-unknown and custom present-option adapter; serializer and adapter bodies were not inspected, so no trait simplification or null behavior claimed.

Signed axial range may intentionally be [0,0] for mount-only shapes; it is a seat coordinate interval and cannot serve as a complete solid bounding box. Material ratio versus physical lengths are separate.
Owner and frame strings encode distinct identity and namespace semantics in observed code; q127 addresses reconstructing owner from alias, not a demand to remove human labels or arbitrary strings.

Mount alignment tolerances and conservative polygon apothem encode physical fit; nominal world-scale, sampling, ratio and final geometry bounds are distinct contracts. No arbitrary new clamp is prescribed.
